claims.text: High-temperature structural stability of multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles is governed by formation of a stable, locally ordered structure.
High-temperature chemical stability of these nanoparticles is governed by formation of a stable, locally ordered structure.
Synthesis temperature influences the formation of the locally ordered structure.
Synthesis pressure influences the formation of the locally ordered structure.
Composition influences the formation of the locally ordered structure.
Systematically varying synthesis temperature, pressure, and composition will produce differences in local ordering that can be observed in situ.
A stable, locally ordered structure will improve nanoparticle structural stability under high-temperature service.
A stable, locally ordered structure will improve nanoparticle chemical stability under high-temperature service.
Improved structural and chemical stability will enhance catalytic performance and suitability.
Improved structural and chemical stability will enhance thermoelectric performance and suitability.
The proposed catalytic-service boundary is 773–1173 K.
The proposed thermoelectric-service boundary is 473–1923 K.
Applicability is limited by noble-metal content.
